newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks fall sharply on "samba effect".
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks fall sharply on "samba effect".

text.p: Mexican share prices opened sharply down on profit-taking coupled with weakness on market heavyweight Telmex, which was a casualty of plunging Brazilian equities, dealers said.
"We were expecting profit-taking, but then they had opened sharply down in Brazil, which took down Telmex and the rest of the market with it," a desk trader said.

Mexico's leading IPC share index was down 39.26 points or 0.82 percent at 4,777.11, in the opening minutes of trade. In Sao Paulo, the Bovespa index of most active stocks dived 5.04 percent to 11,137 points.
Dealers said telecoms stock Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) was susceptible to weakness in its Brazilian counterpart, Telebras, which was leading the slide in Sao Paulo.
Telmex fell by 70 centavos in the early minutes of dealing to 19.80 percent, and apart from cross trades accounted for about one-third of shares traded in early dealing.
Traders pointed out that some blue chips had withstood the downdraft from Brazil and that volume on the Mexican market of 2.9 million shares showed dealing was cautious.
"We've been hit, but it's not a sell-off yet," a floor trader said.
Industrial conglomerate Alfa edged up 10 centavos to 57.10 pesos, while tobacco and agribusiness holding company Moderna was up 5 centavos at 47.00 pesos.

Traders said the two stocks, which are both included in the IPC, may have gained on positioning ahead of second quarter earnings, but noted they had moved at thin volume which did not underpin a definite market trend.
On the broad market, sliders outnumbered gainers by 20 to five, out of a total of 33 stocks traded.
